body: My 18-month-old has started hitting when he's frustrated. We've tried redirecting and saying 'gentle hands' but it doesn't seem to be working. Any tips from parents who've been through this? I'm worried he'll start hitting other kids at daycare.

Just brought home our second baby and our 3-year-old is having a really hard time adjusting. Lots of regression and acting out. The guilt is real — I feel like I'm failing both of them. How did you help your older child transition to being a big sibling?

My 8-year-old's school is introducing AI tutors this year. I'm honestly torn — part of me is excited about the personalised learning, but I'm also worried about screen time and whether a machine can really understand my child's emotional needs. Has anyone else's school done this? How did it go?

We decided to delay kindergarten for our summer-born 5-year-old. Best decision we ever made. He's now more confident, socially ready, and genuinely excited about school. Sharing this because I know how agonising this decision can be — happy to answer any questions about the process.

My 9-year-old came home in tears because someone told her she was 'weird' for liking science instead of TikTok dances. We had a long talk about how the kids who are 'weird' now are the ones who change the world later. But it still broke my heart. How do you help your kids stay true to themselves?

First-time mom here at 32 weeks! Starting to get those 'oh my gosh what have we done' panic moments. Any advice on what you wish someone had told you before your first arrived? Trying to prepare without spiralling into over-research mode 😅

Found my 13-year-old's TikTok account and some of the content is... not what I was expecting. Nothing dangerous, but definitely more mature than I thought she was interested in. How do I bring this up without her feeling like I invaded her privacy? She doesn't know I found it.

Screen time win! We started using the 'tech together' approach — only watching shows with our 2-year-old and talking about what we see. Her language exploded and she actually asks to turn it off when she's done. Sharing because I was so skeptical but it really worked for us.

Can we normalise formula feeding without the guilt? My milk never came in properly and I spent 6 weeks in tears trying to breastfeed before switching. My baby is thriving, I'm happier, and I wish someone had told me earlier that fed is best. Full stop.

My 4-year-old asked me 'Mummy, why is your tummy soft?' and I said 'Because it stretched to hold you when you were growing inside me, and that's my favourite thing about it.' She hugged my tummy and said 'I love your soft tummy.' These are the moments that make all the hard days worth it 💛

Just had parent-teacher conferences. My 7-year-old's teacher said she's 'a joy to have in class' and I almost cried right there in the tiny chair. After all the big feelings and hard bedtimes at home, knowing she's kind in the world outside means everything.

Research update: A new longitudinal study (n=2,400) found that children who use AI tools with parental co-viewing show better critical thinking outcomes than solo users. The key isn't restricting AI — it's engaging with it together. Happy to discuss the findings and practical strategies in the replies.
